description: Meta sits mid-transition between two interview loops in 2026. The legacy track still drives most candidates through CodeSignal-style OAs and tightly time-boxed coding rounds, while a new AI-Native loop layers in AI-assisted coding, AI-Enabled system design, and an AI-oriented behavioral round on top. Which track you land in depends on org and recruiter, not candidate preference.
note: Question block only. The site's answer body is not included here; the untouched page is kept verbatim in raw/<slug>.txt.

questions.title: AI Coding — Maze Solver
questions.overview: Meta's signature AI-Enabled Coding prompt. 4-5 progressive sub-tasks on a grid-maze codebase, building from bug-fix to BFS to key/door bitmask state to a Q5 bomb-blast variant added in April.

questions.title: AI Coding — Maximum Unique Character Subset
questions.overview: Given a list of words, pick a subset whose combined characters are all unique and cover the maximum number of distinct letters. Progressive sub-tasks push backtracking to bitmask + state-compression DP on word lists in the 10k range.

questions.title: CodeSignal OA — Banking System (Progressive OOD)
questions.overview: CodeSignal 90-minute, 4-level Progressive OOD. Banking-system variant: create accounts, deposit, transfer; top-spenders ranking; scheduled payments; merge accounts with historical-balance queries.

questions.title: Random Pick with Weight
questions.overview: LeetCode 528. Sample an index proportional to its weight. Prefix-sum + binary-search is the LC answer; Meta's MLE follow-up pushes you to the Alias Method for O(1)-per-call sampling under millions of calls.

questions.title: Valid Palindrome II
questions.overview: LeetCode 680 / 1216. Two-pointer with a single allowed deletion (or K deletions in the harder follow-up). Meta-canon phone-screen problem.

questions.title: Lowest Common Ancestor (BT / BST / N-ary)
questions.overview: LeetCode 235 (BST), 236 (binary tree), and 1644 (with optional nodes). The N-ary variant is Meta's preferred follow-up.

questions.title: Min Remove to Make Valid Parentheses
questions.overview: LeetCode 1249. Stack-based scan removing minimum parens to make the string valid. Multi-bracket-type extension is the canonical follow-up.

questions.title: Find Peak Element
questions.overview: LeetCode 162. Binary search for any peak in an array where `nums[i] != nums[i+1]`. Edge-handling at boundaries is the differentiator.

questions.title: AI Coding — Friend Recommendation
questions.overview: Starter codebase exposes a `User` class with `friends` and `valid_recommend` helpers. Three sub-tasks build from logic-bug fix to AI-assisted random recommender to mutual-friends Top-K ranking.

questions.title: Binary Tree Vertical Order / Right Side View
questions.overview: LeetCode 314 (Vertical Order Traversal) and LeetCode 199 (Right Side View). Phone-screen staple, frequently asked as a paired combo (left view + right view) or as the vertical-order traversal with deterministic ordering.

questions.title: AI Coding — Card Game (Three Cards Summing to 15)
questions.overview: Card game with 36 cards (4 suits × values 1-9). Starting table has 16 random cards; each round pick 3 cards summing to 15 for 15 points, then refill until no more pairs are possible. Perfect score is 12 pairs × 15 = 180. Four progressive sub-tasks: debug a draw method → naive scorer → simulate to measure quality → optimize with DP.

questions.title: Kth Largest Element / Quick Select
questions.overview: LeetCode 215 (Kth Largest Element in an Array). Phone-screen workhorse — heap or in-place quickselect, with the streaming-Kth variant as a typical follow-up.

questions.title: Sum Root-to-Leaf Numbers
questions.overview: Solve the LC 129 prompt: treat each root-to-leaf sequence of digits as a number and return the sum of all such numbers. Follow-ups compare recursive and iterative traversal and ask what happens when the tree is very deep.

questions.title: Shortest Path in a Binary Matrix (LC 1091)
questions.overview: Starting from the LC 1091 binary-grid prompt, find a path from the top-left cell to the bottom-right and then print the route. The follow-up rejects carrying a full path in every queue entry and asks for a more space-efficient reconstruction.

questions.title: Number of Islands API Variant
questions.overview: Given a binary grid, implement `isSizeExist(int size)` to answer whether any island has exactly the requested area. Precompute complete component sizes once, then answer each query from the resulting set.

questions.title: Tally Service
questions.overview: Implement a Tally Service with `bump(timestamp)` to record an event and `query(startTime, endTime)` to return the inclusive count for a time range. Follow-ups require thread-safe high-concurrency behavior, bounded memory through a sliding window or time buckets, and faster queries.

questions.title: Randomized Container
questions.overview: Implement a generic container with `insert(T element)` and `popRandom()`, where `popRandom` removes and returns one stored element with equal probability. The expected implementation keeps insertion and random removal at O(1).

questions.title: Attention Implementation + Flash / Linear Attention Follow-ups
questions.overview: Implement the standard attention computation in code, analyze its time and space complexity, then answer oral follow-ups on FlashAttention and linear attention. This appears in a Meta Superintelligence / MLE-style loop alongside research-design and ML-foundations rounds.

questions.title: Shortest Unique Prefix
questions.overview: For each word in a list, return the shortest prefix that uniquely distinguishes it from every other word, preserving the original input order. Solved with a Trie tracking per-node pass counts. The variant seen guaranteed that no word is a prefix of another, which drops one class of edge cases.

questions.title: Valid Number
questions.overview: Classic LC 65 — decide whether a string is a valid number (integer, decimal, with optional sign, optional `e`/`E` exponent). Surfaced as the warm-up in a recent E5 phone screen with light wording changes.

questions.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
questions.overview: LC 121 — maximum profit from a single buy / sell of a stock price array. Asked in a recent E5 onsite coding round, with a follow-up extending to multiple transactions.

questions.title: Group Anagrams
questions.overview: Classic LC 49 — bucket strings into anagram groups. Surfaced in a recent Sr SDE phone screen as the warm-up.

questions.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
questions.overview: Classic LC 19 — remove the Nth-from-end node of a singly-linked list in one pass. Asked as the second phone-screen problem in a Sr SDE loop.

questions.title: Continuous Subarray Sum
questions.overview: LC 523 — find a contiguous subarray (length ≥ 2) whose sum is a multiple of `k`. Asked as the second E5 phone-screen problem.

questions.title: Minimum Add to Make Parentheses Valid
questions.overview: LC 921 — count the minimum insertions (of `(` or `)`) needed to make a parens string valid. Surfaced as the first E5 phone-screen problem.

questions.title: Minimum Window Substring
questions.overview: LC 76 — find the shortest substring of `s` that contains every character of `t` (counts respected). Asked as the second phone-screen problem in a recent SWE loop; missing the optimal-window approach gets the candidate dropped.

questions.title: AI Project Round (Take-Home-Style)
questions.overview: Pilot Meta round (Feb 2026): a multi-hour AI-assisted project session. 30-min intro to a mock full-stack app, ~1 hour solo implementation with any AI tools, ~1.5-hour interviewer walkthrough + live feature extension.

questions.title: LRU Cache
questions.overview: LeetCode 146. O(1) get/put with capacity eviction. Doubly-linked list + hashmap is the canonical implementation; an MLE/SDE onsite warm-up.

questions.title: CodeSignal OA — In-Memory Database
questions.overview: Implement an in-memory database with record operations, filtered scans, timestamps, and TTL. A later variant adds get_when(key, field, at) to retrieve a field’s historical value instead of restoring the entire database.

questions.title: Range Sum of BST
questions.overview: LeetCode 938. DFS through a BST summing nodes whose values fall in `[low, high]`. Pruning via BST property is the discussion point.

questions.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
questions.overview: LeetCode 560. Count subarrays whose sum equals K. Prefix-sum + hashmap is the canonical solution; appears as the second half of Meta phone screens paired with a heavier first problem.

questions.title: Dinosaur Speed (Meta PE classic)
questions.overview: Meta Production Engineer classic. Given timestamps when dinosaurs cross sensor lines, pair them up so each pair represents the same dinosaur, and compute speeds. Time-window pairing + binary search.

questions.title: Minimum Round-Trip Flight Cost
questions.overview: Given parallel arrays of departure and return flight prices, choose a departure day strictly before the return day to minimize total cost. Return both indices; when several pairs have the same minimum cost, prefer the earliest departure and the latest return. The round explicitly asks for an O(n^2) baseline followed by an O(n) optimization.

questions.title: Basic Calculator I / II
questions.overview: LeetCode 224 / 227. Evaluate arithmetic expressions from a string. Stack-based evaluation with operator precedence; Meta-variant adds extra rules around eval order or unary operators.

questions.title: AI Coding — Shared Substring in String List
questions.overview: AI-Enabled Coding variant outside the Maze / Card-Game canon: given a list of strings, find a string that contains another from the list as a substring (or any pair sharing a substring relationship), then improve beyond brute force across 2-3 successive approaches.

questions.title: Walls and Gates / Max Area of Island
questions.overview: LeetCode 286 (Walls and Gates) and LC 695 (Max Area of Island). Multi-source BFS for the distance-fill variant; matrix DFS for the area variant. Both surface as standard grid-traversal warm-ups at Meta.

questions.title: DE AI-Native Full-Stack Round
questions.overview: Single 60-min Data Engineer round threading Business Case + Data Modeling + SQL + Python through one continuous scenario. AI is allowed in most sections but disallowed for SQL.

questions.title: Pow(x, n)
questions.overview: LeetCode 50. Fast-exponentiation `x^n` with negative-exponent handling. Classic Meta phone-screen warm-up.

questions.title: Alien Dictionary
questions.overview: LeetCode 269. Given a list of words sorted in an unknown alphabet's lexicographic order, return a valid letter ordering. Build a precedence graph from adjacent word pairs, run topological sort.

questions.title: AI Coding — Compiler Optimization
questions.overview: A new April-2026 AI Coding prompt. Implement `extract_time_and_mem_cost(instruction_file)` for a toy compiler IR. Catch: instruction costs are not given — they must be inferred from the unit-test assertions.

questions.title: Tree Diameter / Longest Path
questions.overview: LeetCode 543 / 1245. Longest path between any two nodes in a tree. DFS returns the deepest descendant chain; at each node, the diameter candidate is the sum of the two longest child chains.

questions.title: Mouse and Cheese / Maze Rewards
questions.overview: Meta-classic DP-on-grid: maximize reward collected along a path from corner to corner. Two confirmed variants — a memo-DP version, and an API-exploration version where only `move()` / `canMove()` are exposed (no global view).

questions.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
questions.overview: LeetCode 128. Find the length of the longest consecutive-integer subsequence in an unsorted array. The trick is the O(n) hashset solution that only expands from sequence-starts.

questions.title: System Design — Facebook Search (Mini Elasticsearch)
questions.overview: Design Facebook post search — given query terms, return all matching posts. The exercise is essentially "build a mini Elasticsearch": inverted index, ranking, top-K per query, real-time ingestion.

questions.title: MLSD — Harmful / Weapon-Sales Content Detection
questions.overview: Integrity-style MLSD: detect harmful content (weapon sales, harmful ads) at scale. Weak labels, active learning, policy alignment, and precision-recall trade-offs are the live discussion points.

questions.title: MLSD — Nearby Place Recommendation
questions.overview: Location-aware recommender for nearby places (Marketplace shops, FB Places). Geohash retrieval + mobile real-time constraints + context features distinguish it from generic feed MLSD.

questions.title: MLSD — Reels / Short Video Recommendation
questions.overview: Design the Reels short-video recommender. Four-stage retrieval → pre-rank → rank → re-rank scaffold is table stakes; differentiation is in features, metrics, and A/B-test design.

questions.title: MLSD — Ads Ranking
questions.overview: Design the Meta ads-ranking system. Feature engineering, model architecture, and calibration are the three deep-dive zones reported.

questions.title: System Design — Instagram / News Feed
questions.overview: Classic Meta SD prompt. Design Instagram or Facebook News Feed with personalized ranking. Push vs pull fan-out, hot-key handling, and a ranking layer are the canonical decision points.

questions.title: System Design — Online Auction / eBay
questions.overview: Auction with concurrent bidding, real-time price updates, and close-out semantics. Pub/sub + SSE-pushed bid notifications and queue-partitioning by auction-id are the canonical answer.

questions.title: AI-Enabled System Design — Agent System
questions.overview: New round introduced April 16, 2026 in the AI-Native full loop. Design an LLM-agent system for an automation task (auto-ticket-triage and code-review agent are confirmed prompts). ReAct-loop vs multi-agent decomposition + cost / memory / tool design are the live drill-downs.

questions.title: System Design — Trending Hashtags
questions.overview: Design a backend system that detects and serves trending hashtags from Facebook posts. The system must surface trends while the real-world event is happening, target about 1-minute latency, consider the last 24 hours of posts with recency weighting, reward popularity across the community, and distinguish genuinely novel spikes from long-running background chatter.

questions.title: MLSD — Image Copyright Violation Detection
questions.overview: Detect whether a user-uploaded image violates copyright. VLM embedding + ANN lookup is the consensus retrieval approach; the interesting depth lives in adversarial robustness and partial-violation follow-ups.

questions.title: System Design — Web Crawler / Google Flight
questions.overview: Distributed web crawler at Meta scale, occasionally framed as Google Flight price aggregator. URL frontier, DAG scheduling, politeness rules, and storage are the standard deep-dive zones.

questions.title: System Design — Ticketmaster / Ticketing
questions.overview: Ticket-purchase system: seat inventory, hold/reserve flow, flash-sale concurrency. Reservation TTL + distributed locking is the central trade-off.

questions.title: System Design — LeetCode / Online Judge + Contest Leaderboard
questions.overview: Design an online code-judge with a contest leaderboard. Sandbox execution, judging pipeline, and real-time leaderboard updates are the three drill-down zones.

questions.title: MLSD — Notification Ranking (Multi-source)
questions.overview: Rank notifications from heterogeneous sources (friend activity, ads, system) under a unified objective. Multi-objective ranking + frequency-cap + value-normalization across sources are the deep-dive axes.

questions.title: Traditional Behavioral — Meta
questions.overview: Meta's classic 45-min BQ round. Heavy on project-deepening: ambiguity, conflict, most-proud project, role models, self-improvement. L6+ candidates face a markedly different bar focused on org-level scope and influence-without-authority.

questions.title: AI-Oriented Behavioral (AI BQ, NEW)
questions.overview: New behavioral round in the post-April-16 AI-Native loop. Standard STAR-shaped questions reweighted toward AI-tool collaboration, prompt judgment, and recognizing AI failure modes.

questions.title: ML Foundations — Optimizers, Scaling Laws, K-Means and GMM
questions.overview: A machine-learning foundations round covering optimizers, scaling laws, k-means clustering, and Gaussian Mixture Models. The leaked detail is topic-level rather than full question text, so treat this as a drill checklist for an oral fundamentals round.

questions.title: PE Troubleshooting — Web Server / Disk Full
questions.overview: Meta Production Engineer signature round. Interviewer states a production incident (web server down, disk full, customers failing) and you drive the diagnosis step by step — pure Linux/SRE skills, no code.
